name: Editorial magazine cartoon
style_en: witty magazine cartoon in dip-pen ink, printed in exactly three flat colors and nothing else: warm near-black ink (#2B2A28), paper cream (#F4EEE4) and muted slate blue (#4B638E); every original color is translated into these three, and each outfit is split across all three so no figure is dressed in a single color: dark garments (burgundy, navy, olive, charcoal) become solid near-black or slate blue, light or muted garments (cream, white, sage, light denim) become cream with a few ink hatch lines, bright garments (mustard, orange, teal) become slate blue, small yellow items become cream with an ink outline; there is no yellow, orange, green, red, tan or brown anywhere; skin is shown only as ink density: pale skin stays cream, light-brown skin is a light warm ink wash, deep-brown skin is a dense near-black wash with small cream highlights; the figure is a loose caricature about five heads tall with a large head, narrow shoulders, long thin legs and small simplified hands; the face is four or five nib strokes only (two small almond eyes, a one-line nose, a short mouth), no lashes, no lip color, no rendered shading; lively dip-pen contour with thick-thin swell and sparse cross-hatching; slate-blue proofreader's marks (circles, underlines, arrows, carets and margin brackets) drawn around the figure as if by a copy editor; no brand logos
nothing_around: Nothing floats around the figure: no proofreader's marks, circles, arrows, brackets or carets this time.
